🇲🇽🛢️ <u>HOW THE 4T REBUILT MEXICO'S ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY — $20 BILLION AND COUNTING</u>

The neoliberal fire-sale is over. Under AMLO, Mexico poured more than $20 billion into energy sovereignty: 13 new combined-cycle plants adding ~18,000 MW, 3,500+ km of transmission lines, 190 substations built or rehabilitated, 20 modernized hydro plants, the Olmeca refinery, and 100% ownership of the Deer Park refinery in Texas. Contralínea's read: it restored "the State's capacity to lead a sector considered strategic" — reliable supply for 130 million people.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>THE FBI PUT EL MAYO'S PLANE IN A MUSEUM — AND BLEW SALAZAR'S ALIBI</u>

The smoking gun: the aircraft used to fly "El Mayo" Zambada out of Mexico now sits in a New Mexico aviation museum — donated by the FBI itself, presented as one of the Bureau's own operations. Back in August 2024, ambassador Ken Salazar swore "it wasn't our plane, our pilot, or our operation." President Sheinbaum's read on the exhibit: "Todo parece indicar que Ken Salazar mintió" — everything indicates Ken Salazar lied.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO FORMALLY ACCUSES THE FBI OF LYING OVER 'EL MAYO' ABDUCTION</u>

Mexico's FGR just formally accused Washington of lying. Attorney General Ernestina Godoy says the FBI handed Mexico "false or imprecise" information about the July 2024 abduction of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada — this after 7 open investigations, 153 interviews, 1,288 reports and 124 expert assessments, with altered aircraft-ID logs on record. If the FBI ran the operation on Mexican soil without telling Mexico, Godoy says, it violated the UN Charter, the OAS Charter, Mexico's Constitution and its National Security Law.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>IMF cuts Mexico's forecast to 1.2%, citing 'uncertainty' — the same week it cut the whole world</u>

The IMF trimmed Mexico's 2026 growth outlook from 1.6% to 1.2%, blaming "uncertainty," in the same July report that cut GLOBAL growth to 3% over a Middle East war Washington started and ended. Sheinbaum's reply: there is no uncertainty — record formal employment (22.7M), record exports to the US ($54B in May alone), and FDI back in the world's top 10. The uncertainty is made in Washington, not Mexico City.

🇲🇽♀️ <u>Mexico City enacts a Care System Law — care as a right, unpaid domestic work finally counted</u>

Mayor Clara Brugada promulgated a first-of-its-kind Care System Law that recognizes care as a right and puts an economic value on the unpaid domestic labor women have always carried — delivered through public "Utopías" and neighborhood care houses. "The construction of a welfare state with a feminist perspective," she said. The market never paid for this work. The 4T is.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico hits a record 22.7 million formal jobs</u>

IMSS registered 22,779,704 formal jobs in June — up 454,000 from a year ago, the strongest annual gain in 23 months. Women hold 9.2 million of them (40.4%), and 237,000 gig-platform workers now have full social security for the first time. Labor productivity grew 1.96% — triple the OECD average. This is the economy the IMF keeps calling "uncertain."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>First Indigenous chief justice: ejido and Indigenous land are not 'second-category' property</u>

Mexico's new Supreme Court president Hugo Aguilar Ortiz told the Agrarian Procuracy that communal land can no longer be treated as "second or third category" next to private property, and that consultation with affected communities is a constitutional right. "If we deliver sentences but not solutions, the judicial reform will have been worthless." Elected judges, Indigenous land rights as doctrine — this is what the reform was for.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico climbs back into the world's top 10 for foreign investment</u>

Despite a year of tariff threats from Washington, Mexico returned to the top 10 global destinations for foreign direct investment in 2025 — $41 billion, per UNCTAD's World Investment Report, up from 11th place ($38B) the year before. Capital doesn't move toward a country it doesn't trust. Nearshoring runs through Mexico, not around it.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico dismantles a 'railway huachicol' fuel-smuggling network — customs agents included</u>

The FGR and Security Cabinet took down a scheme that moved illicit fuel through Matamoros customs using shell companies, importers, logistics operators and complicit customs agents. Seized: 170 rail tankers holding 18.9 million liters — a 239-million-peso hit to the operation, with 70+ people and firms under investigation across nine states. The fuel-theft machine the old regime fed on is being pulled apart piece by piece.

🌐🐉🇲🇽 The queue to join BRICS now runs through Latin America

India takes the BRICS chair in 2026 and will host the 18th summit in New Delhi on September 12–13, where a second wave of expansion is expected. Nearly 65 countries across Latin America and Asia have applications or interest on the table — the bloc already spans 11 members and 10 partners, with Brazil, Bolivia and Cuba giving the region a foothold.

The pull is material, not ideological. China–Latin America trade hit a record $518 billion, Beijing has dangled a $9 billion regional credit line, and currency-swap and local-currency deals are quietly routing trade around the dollar. The theme of India’s presidency — “South–South cooperation” — is a polite way of saying the Global South is building doors that don’t open onto Washington.

For Mexico the lesson isn’t “pick a camp.” It’s that the world now has more than one door. Every new bloc and every new partner is one more option a single northern neighbor can no longer take off the table. That is what sovereignty looks like in a multipolar century.
